title: The Compass of the Lower Danube
premise: In 1848, on the eve of revolution, Mirabel Sandoval completes the atlas her murdered master died protecting — a map that secretly charts escape routes along the Lower Danube for those fleeing imperial census and conscription. When a census taker's probing questions expose her, Mirabel inherits both the atlas and the network of smugglers, ferrymen, and forgers who guarded it. As orders come down to seize 'unregistered persons,' she must decide who among her found family takes the last berth on the final boat downstream. She chooses to give up her own place, forging a new identity into the atlas itself, and ends the book steering the map — and the survivors — toward the delta and an uncertain freedom.
about_author: Casper Amberdale is the pen name of a former cartographic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing river charts of southeastern Europe before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about people whose lives are measured in inches of paper and miles of water.

chapters.title: The Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel Sandoval, POV. In her dead master's workshop she inks the final plate of his atlas, hiding escape routes inside decorative borders. The emotional beat is grief braided with purpose: she finishes what he died for while pretending it is only geography.

chapters.title: A Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A census taker named Herr Vogel arrives, courteous and relentless, asking not just names but loyalties and origins. He lingers over the workshop's maps. The beat is dread: one careless answer about her master's 'river clients' puts her on a list.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Danilo, an aging ferryman. He reveals her master's secret: the atlas is a guidebook for the unregistered fleeing down the Danube. The beat is reluctant inheritance — Mirabel realizes the maps were never meant for sale.

chapters.title: Orders Come Down
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Imperial edicts demand registration of all persons without papers; soldiers begin house searches. Vogel returns with a warrant for the atlas. The beat is panic compressed into decision: burn it, or become its keeper.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She dismantles the atlas into portable pieces — plates disguised as wallpaper, routes memorized, names sewn into her coat hem. The beat is quiet resolve; measuring the world by what fits in two hands.

chapters.title: The House of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: New POV: Ilka, a forger who owed Mirabel's master. She shelters Mirabel and introduces the network — smugglers, priests, barge crews. The beat is wary belonging: strangers becoming something like family.

chapters.title: Vogel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vogel's POV, first time. We see the machinery of the census: lists, informants, quotas. He suspects the atlas exists and begins hunting its 'ghost routes.' The beat is chilling competence — the antagonist is patient, not cruel.

chapters.title: Downstream at Night
chapters.summary: Danilo's POV. The first convoy: twelve fugitives moved by barge under falsified grain manifests, guided by Mirabel's memorized route. The beat is terror turning to awe as her lines on paper become real safe passage.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Counted Stars
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She takes in Tomas, an orphaned stowaway who navigates by stars better than any chart. The beat is tenderness hardening into responsibility — he becomes the little brother she never chose but now cannot lose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Mill
chapters.summary: Ilka's POV. An informant inside the network sells a rendezvous point; three are taken. The beat is guilt and suspicion — someone close talked, and every bond now carries a question mark.

chapters.title: The Price of Paper
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Forged papers cost more than coin now; Ilka demands the atlas's original plates as payment. Mirabel must weigh the mission against the artifact her master died for. The beat is sacrifice of the sacred for the living.

chapters.title: Quarantine at Silistra
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A river checkpoint strands the convoy; disease rumors give guards excuse to detain everyone. The beat is claustrophobic fear, broken when Tomas's star-reading finds an unmarked channel past the patrol boats.

chapters.title: Vogel Closes In
chapters.summary: Vogel's POV. He traces the ghost routes to their source and identifies 'the apprentice.' He offers Mirabel immunity in exchange for the network's names. The beat is temptation with a human face — he genuinely believes order is mercy.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She meets Vogel in a customs house and refuses, reciting the names of the taken as her answer. The beat is defiant clarity: she stops being an apprentice and becomes the atlas herself.

chapters.title: Broken Compass
chapters.summary: Danilo's POV. The informant is exposed — it was not treachery but coercion; his family was held. The network fractures over whether to forgive him. The beat is moral complexity: justice outside the law must still be just.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The final boat has room for exactly one more than they have people — no, one berth fewer than souls. Soldiers approach. The blurb's choice arrives: Mirabel begins deciding who stays behind. The beat is unbearable arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Vote at Midnight
chapters.summary: Ilka's POV. Instead of choosing alone, Mirabel puts the decision to the found family — and each person argues someone else should go. The beat is love expressed as refusal of rescue.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She engraves a new plate overnight: her own identity dissolved into the atlas, a forged passage bearing her name given to Tomas. The beat is self-erasure as the ultimate act of authorship.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs converging. Vogel raids the dock as the boat casts off; Danilo rams the patrol skiff, Ilka burns the ledger archive, and Mirabel slips away upstream with the atlas, drawing pursuit after her. The beat is chaos transfigured into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Delta
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The survivors reach the delta's reed labyrinth under stars he can read. They carry Mirabel's routes in memory now. The beat is grief and arrival entwined — freedom bought, not given.

chapters.title: What the Map Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Vogel's POV. He captures an empty workshop and a decoy atlas, realizing too late the true map was always people. The beat is ambiguous defeat: he files his report, but something in him has begun to doubt the ledger.

chapters.title: Compass of the Lower Danube
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue. Months later, upstream in a new town under a borrowed name, she teaches Tomas and others to draw the routes from memory. The beat is resolution: the atlas lives on in hands, not pages — a family drawn together by lines on water.
